proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\eta\), \(k_0\), and \(P\) as in the theorem.  By \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), the labeled global fiber is nonempty and every member has exactly the displayed control collision and the other three terminal differences nonzero.  For \(\psi\in\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\), define the arm-conditional latent prefix mass and terminal probability by
\[
 R_{zd}^{\psi}(i,j,k)
 =w_{zd}B(u_{zd};i)B(a_{zi};j)B(\kappa_{zd3j};k),
 \qquad v_{zdk}^{\psi}=\kappa_{zd4k}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Summing first over latent type and then after multiplication by the conditional probability of \(X_4=1\) gives
\[
 H_d(i,j,k)=R_{1d}^{\psi}(i,j,k)+R_{2d}^{\psi}(i,j,k),
 \qquad
 N_d(i,j,k)=v_{1dk}^{\psi}R_{1d}^{\psi}(i,j,k)+v_{2dk}^{\psi}R_{2d}^{\psi}(i,j,k).
 \tag{2}
\]
Every Bernoulli factor in the model is at least \(\eta\).  Also \(p_d=\sum_z\pi_zB(e_z;d)\in[\eta,U]\).  Consequently
\[
 w_{zd}=\frac{\pi_zB(e_z;d)}{p_d}\geq\frac{\eta^2}{U}
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 R_{zd}^{\psi}(i,j,k)\geq\frac{\eta^5}{U}>\eta^5.
 \tag{3}
\]
This proves every positivity assertion used below.

At \((d,k)=(0,k_0)\), the defining collision gives \(v_{10k_0}^{\psi}=v_{20k_0}^{\psi}\).  Equation (2) therefore implies
\[
 N_0(i,j,k_0)=v_{10k_0}^{\psi}H_0(i,j,k_0).
\]
The three displayed collision minors vanish and, because \(H_0(0,0,k_0)>0\),
\[
 v_{10k_0}^{\psi}=v_{20k_0}^{\psi}
 =\frac{N_0(0,0,k_0)}{H_0(0,0,k_0)}.
 \tag{4}
\]
The four values \(R_{10}^{\psi}(i,j,k_0)\) remain free.  In every other block, the terminal difference is nonzero; solving the two linear equations in (2) gives
\[
 R_{1d}^{\psi}(i,j,k)
 =\frac{N_d(i,j,k)-v_{2dk}^{\psi}H_d(i,j,k)}{v_{1dk}^{\psi}-v_{2dk}^{\psi}},
 \qquad R_{2d}^{\psi}(i,j,k)=H_d(i,j,k)-R_{1d}^{\psi}(i,j,k).
 \tag{5}
\]
Choose the three entries of \(s\) to be the signs of these differences.  There are \(2^3\) possible orientations.

For each \((z,d,j)\), factorization (1) yields
\[
 R_{zd}^{\psi}(0,j,0)R_{zd}^{\psi}(1,j,1)
 -R_{zd}^{\psi}(0,j,1)R_{zd}^{\psi}(1,j,0)=0,
 \tag{6}
\]
which gives the eight equations \(\rho_{zdj}=0\).  Label the treated arm components by \(z\), and let control arm-local component \(\sigma(z)\) represent the same structural type.  Sharing \(a_{zi}\) across arms and using (3) gives
\[
 \frac{T_{\sigma(z),0}^{R^{\psi}}(i,1)}{S_{\sigma(z),0}^{R^{\psi}}(i)}
 =\frac{T_{z1}^{R^{\psi}}(i,1)}{S_{z1}^{R^{\psi}}(i)}.
\]
Cross multiplication is legitimate and gives the four equations \(\gamma_{zi}^{\sigma}(R^{\psi})=0\).  All reconstructed coordinates are the corresponding coordinates of \(\psi\), after the explicit control relabeling by \(\sigma\), and hence satisfy every box sign.  Equations (3)--(6) therefore put the six noncollided terminal probabilities and the four collided-block splits into one of the sixteen solution sets.  The corrected reconstruction returns \(\psi\).  This proves that the chart union maps onto the labeled fiber.

Conversely, let \(y\) satisfy \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\), and construct \(R\) and \(v\) from the splitting formulas.  The orientation signs make the three denominators in (5) nonzero.  The imposed lower bounds make every \(R_{zd}(i,j,k)\), and hence every \(T_{zd}^{R}(i,j)\), \(S_{zd}^{R}(i)\), and \(w_{zd}^{R}\), positive.  The first identity in (2), which now holds by construction, yields \(\sum_z w_{zd}^{R}=1\).

For fixed \((z,d,j)\), positivity and \(\rho_{zdj}=0\) say that the two rows of the positive \(2\)-by-\(2\) array in \((i,k)\) have the same normalized \(k\)-distribution.  With
\[
 \kappa_{zd3j}^{R}=\frac{R_{zd}(0,j,1)}{T_{zd}^{R}(0,j)},
\]
one therefore has
\[
 R_{zd}(i,j,k)=T_{zd}^{R}(i,j)B(\kappa_{zd3j}^{R};k).
 \tag{7}
\]
The definitions of \(u_{zd}^{R}\) and \(a_{zdi}^{R}\) similarly give
\[
 T_{zd}^{R}(i,j)=w_{zd}^{R}B(u_{zd}^{R};i)B(a_{zdi}^{R};j).
 \tag{8}
\]
Because all \(S\)'s are positive, the four alignment equations are equivalent to
\[
 a_{\sigma(z),0,i}^{R}=a_{z1i}^{R}.
 \tag{9}
\]
Use the corrected reconstruction: structural type \(z\) takes its treated primitives from arm-local component \(z\), its control primitives from arm-local component \(\sigma(z)\), and the common quantity in (9) as \(a_{zi}\).  Finally set
\[
 \pi_z=p_0w_{\sigma(z),0}^{R}+p_1w_{z1}^{R},
 \qquad e_z=\frac{p_1w_{z1}^{R}}{\pi_z}.
 \tag{10}
\]
All terms are positive, and
\[
 \pi_ze_z=p_1w_{z1}^{R},\qquad
 \pi_z(1-e_z)=p_0w_{\sigma(z),0}^{R},\qquad
 \sum_z\pi_z=p_0+p_1=1.
 \tag{11}
\]
The imposed box signs put every reconstructed structural primitive in \([\eta,U]\), so the reconstruction belongs to \(\Theta_\eta\).  Combining (7), (8), and (11) reconstructs the conditional prefix factors in \(F\).  The two identities (2) then reconstruct all cells with \(X_4=1\), and subtraction from \(H_d\) reconstructs those with \(X_4=0\).  Multiplication by \(p_d\) gives \(F(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y))=P\).  Equation (4) and the three strict orientation signs give exactly the required one-collision pattern.  Thus every chart solution reconstructs a member of \(\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).

There are two free terminal values in each of the three noncollided blocks and none in the collided block, whose common value is fixed by (4).  There are four free prefix splits in the collided block; all remaining entries of the original thirty-two-dimensional \(R\) are fixed by (2).  Hence the forty coordinates \((R,v)\) reduce to ten.  For fixed \(k_0\), there are eight orientations and two relative alignments, hence sixteen labeled branches; the two choices of \(k_0\) give thirty-two.  No rank matrix is inverted.  Rank failure is retained by (6), all vanishing coefficients are retained as zero polynomial cells, and box contacts are retained by weak inequalities.  The only divisions are by the positive quantities proved above or by an explicitly orientation-signed nonzero terminal difference.  Thus no listed boundary or rank case creates an omitted branch.

Fix \(\eta\), \(k_0\), and \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\).  A compatible structural representation exists.  Since every assignment probability is in \([\eta,U]\),
\[
 p_d=\sum_z\pi_zB(e_z;d)\geq\eta>0.
 \tag{12}
\]
Thus \(H_d\) and \(N_d\) are observable rational functions of the thirty-two cells of \(P\), with denominator \(p_d\).  Multiplying by positive powers of \(p_0p_1\) converts every atomic equality or sign in a branch formula into an equivalent polynomial sign condition in \((P,\eta,y)\).  The family is finite because each branch contains finitely many reconstructed primitives and polynomial conditions.

The corrected observable-certificate definition applies the full Collins projection to the entire current polynomial family at every eliminated coordinate.  In particular, it includes the resultant and signed principal subresultant data for every equality--equality pair, as well as for equality--boundary and boundary--boundary pairs.  By the cited CAD quantifier-elimination lemma, the resulting projection and signed lifting table is finite and sign-invariant for every original polynomial, including on zero sections.  Consequently, for every \((s,\sigma)\),
\[
 \exists y\;\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{at least one lifted cell satisfies every atomic sign of that branch.}
 \tag{13}
\]
Necessity holds because a solution occupies one sign-invariant cell.  Sufficiency holds because the retained sample point of an accepted cell satisfies the original conjunction.  Full pairwise projection is essential here: it preserves the simultaneous zero set of all twelve equality polynomials, rather than merely their intersections with inequality boundaries.  Coefficients, discriminants, pairwise resultants, and signed subresultants retain the same equivalence when a leading coefficient, multiple root, rank coefficient, or box-boundary polynomial vanishes.

The dimension-reduction theorem and quotient invariance give the exact image identity
\[
 \mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)
 =\bigcup_{s\in\{-1,1\}^{3}}\ \bigcup_{\sigma\in\Sigma}
 \left\{
 \tau\!\left(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P\right):
 \mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)
 \right\}.
 \tag{14}
\]
This union is nonempty by membership in \(\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\).  Two elements of the right side differ if and only if some two branch solutions \(y,y'\) satisfy
\[
 \sum_{t=3}^{4}\left[
 \tau_t\!\left(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P\right)
 -\tau_t\!\left(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s',\sigma'}(P,y');P\right)
 \right]^2>0.
 \tag{15}
\]
Every denominator in (15) is a product of the positive masses in the reconstruction and the three nonzero terminal differences.  Multiplying by a common squared denominator is therefore sign preserving.  The corrected definition applies the same complete projection and lifting procedure to the conjunction of both branch systems and this strict polynomial inequality, for every pair of labels.  The CAD lemma then says that a comparison formula is accepted exactly when such an unequal pair exists.

If all comparison formulas are rejected, no two elements in the nonempty union (14) differ, so the sharp image is a singleton.  This is equivalently zero within-cell and within-branch oscillation plus equality across all accepted branch and alignment images.  If one comparison formula is accepted, its two retained sample points reconstruct, by the dimension-reduction theorem, two members of the labeled fiber with unequal ATT vectors; quotient invariance shows that they also give two distinct values of the quotient image.  The lifting argument includes every zero section, so this dichotomy remains necessary and sufficient at rank deficiencies, alignment coincidences, and compact-box contacts.

Let \(\eta\) and the cells of \(P\) be rational, with \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,0}^{1\mathrm c}\cup\mathcal M_{\eta,1}^{1\mathrm c}\).  Equation (12) makes both arm probabilities positive.  After clearing the recorded positive denominators, every branch is a finite polynomial sign system with rational coefficients and hence, after common rescaling, integer coefficients.  The algorithm enumerates
\[
 2\cdot2^3\cdot2=32
\]
labels \((k_0,s,\sigma)\).  The cited CAD lemma, applied with the corrected complete projection family, proves termination of each fixed finite projection-and-lifting computation and therefore of the finite loop.

There is a unique \(k_*\in\mathcal A\) for which \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_*}^{1\mathrm c}\): membership for both values would require the same global fiber to have a collision at each control terminal state while also having the other state distinct.  For \(k_0=k_*\), the dimension-reduction theorem and (14) show that the disjunction of accepted branch images is exactly \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).  For \(k_0\ne k_*\), any accepted chart would, by positivity and its eight \(\rho\)-equations, factor \(R\) as in (7)--(8); its four \(\gamma\)-equations would align the arms as in (9); and its weight reconstruction (10)--(11) and terminal split identities would give a structural vector in \(\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).  This would contradict \(\widetilde\Phi_\eta(P)\subseteq\Theta_{\eta,k_*}^{1\mathrm c}\).  Hence every wrong-state chart is rejected and both its branch union and \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\) are empty.  Thus, for each \(k_0\), the algorithm returns the exact image rather than an outer approximation.

Introduce two retained coordinates \((q_3,q_4)\), adjoin
\[
 q_t=\tau_t\!\left(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P\right),
 \qquad t\in\{3,4\},
 \tag{16}
\]
clear only positive denominators, and eliminate \(y\).  The CAD lemma yields an equivalent quantifier-free Boolean combination of integer-polynomial sign conditions in \((q_3,q_4)\).  Taking the disjunction over accepted labels proves the asserted exact joint formula.

For attainment, \(\Theta_\eta\) is compact and \(F\) is continuous, so
\[
 K(P)=\{\psi\in\Theta_\eta:F(\psi)=P\}
\]
is compact.  If \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), exclusivity gives \(K(P)\subseteq\Theta_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), and hence \(K(P)=\widetilde\Phi_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).  The denominator \(p_1\) in \(w_{z1}\) is at least \(\eta\), while the counterfactual recurrences are polynomial in the primitive probabilities.  Thus \(\psi\mapsto\tau(\psi;P)\) is continuous on \(K(P)\).  Its joint image and both coordinate images are compact, and every extreme coordinate value is attained.

Each marginal is semialgebraic by (16) and quantifier elimination.  Collect the finitely many nonzero univariate polynomials appearing in its quantifier-free formula.  Their real roots partition \(\mathbb R\) into finitely many points and open intervals on which every atomic sign is constant.  Compactness therefore makes the selected set a finite ordered union of closed intervals and isolated points.  Rational input makes every boundary root real algebraic.  Square-free factorization, rational root isolation, derivative-sign evaluation, and the signed lifting table produce a square-free integer polynomial, a rational isolating interval, and a Thom sign sequence for each endpoint.

For an endpoint \(q_t\), compactness supplies a point of \(K(P)\) attaining it.  Dimension reduction places that point in an accepted labeled branch.  Equivalently, CAD applied with the section \(q_t\) in (16) lifts to a real-algebraic \(y\); the corrected relabeling reconstruction yields a feasible real-algebraic structural endpoint witness.  If a branch is discarded, completeness of sign-invariant lifting means that every candidate cell violates at least one atomic sign.  Recording the first such atom in every candidate cell gives the finite exact infeasibility certificate promised by the algorithm.  The procedure is precisely real quantifier elimination after the proved ten-coordinate reduction.  Since neither the projection operator nor its generic schedule has been shortened, no improvement in generic worst-case CAD complexity follows.

Fix a cell \(w\) and put \(Y_r=\mathbf 1\{W_r=w\}\) and \(q=P(w)\).  Under independent multinomial sampling, the \(Y_r\)'s are independent Bernoulli variables of mean \(q\).  For every real \(\lambda\),
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\{\lambda(Y_r-q)\}
 =(1-q)e^{-\lambda q}+qe^{\lambda(1-q)}
 \leq e^{\lambda^2/8}.
 \tag{17}
\]
Indeed, if \(K\) is the logarithm of the middle expression, exponential tilting remains Bernoulli, so \(K(0)=K'(0)=0\) and \(K''(\lambda)=q_\lambda(1-q_\lambda)\leq1/4\).  Taylor's formula with integral remainder proves (17).

For any nonnegative \(Z\) and \(a>0\), \(\mathbf 1\{Z\geq a\}\leq Z/a\), so taking expectations gives \(P\{Z\geq a\}\leq \mathbb E[Z]/a\).  Apply this inequality to the exponential of the centered sum.  Independence and (17), for \(\lambda>0\), give
\[
 P^n\{\widehat P_n(w)-P(w)\geq\delta\}
 \leq\exp\{-\lambda n\delta+n\lambda^2/8\}.
\]
Choosing \(\lambda=4\delta\) and applying the same calculation to \(-Y_r\) gives
\[
 P^n\{|\widehat P_n(w)-P(w)|>\delta\}\leq2e^{-2n\delta^2}.
 \tag{18}
\]
There are thirty-two observed cells.  The union bound and the stated value of \(\delta_n(\alpha)\) yield, uniformly over all multinomial laws,
\[
 P^n\{\|\widehat P_n-P\|_\infty>\delta_n(\alpha)\}
 \leq64\exp\{-2n\delta_n(\alpha)^2\}=\alpha.
 \tag{19}
\]
On the complementary event, the true \(P\), which by hypothesis belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), is one of the laws \(Q\) in the union defining \(\mathcal C_{n,k_0}^{\tau}\).  Therefore the whole sharp set \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\), rather than a selected latent value, is contained in \(\mathcal C_{n,k_0}^{\tau}\).  Taking probabilities in (19) and then the infimum over \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\) proves
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}}
 P^n\{\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\subseteq\mathcal C_{n,k_0}^{\tau}\}
 \geq1-\alpha.
\]
Projection of this one joint containment event covers both marginal identified sets simultaneously.  The radius tends to zero, but fixed-coverage containment alone supplies neither lower hemicontinuity nor branch persistence; hence it does not by itself imply the endpoint or Hausdorff conclusions excluded by the theorem.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(k_0\in\mathcal A\) and \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\).  For a branch label \(b=(s,\sigma)\), write \(K_b(Q)=\{y:\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(Q,\eta;y)\}\) and \(g_b(Q,y)=\tau(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(Q,y);Q)\).  Suppose there are a relative neighborhood \(\mathcal V\) of \(P\) in \(\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), a finite index set \(J\), fixed labels \(b(j)\), and nonempty compact connected sets \(K_j(Q)\subseteq K_{b(j)}(Q)\) such that: \(\bigcup_{b}K_b(Q)=\bigcup_{j\in J}K_j(Q)\) for every \(Q\in\mathcal V\); \(d_H(K_j(Q),K_j(P))\to0\) as \(Q\to P\) for every \(j\); and every reconstruction denominator is bounded below in absolute value by one common \(c>0\) on these graphs.  For each \(t\in\{3,4\}\), also suppose there is a fixed partition \(J=J_{t1}\sqcup\cdots\sqcup J_{tm_t}\) such that, throughout \(\mathcal V\), each union \(\bigcup_{j\in J_{tr}}\operatorname{proj}_t g_{b(j)}(Q,K_j(Q))\) is an interval and consecutive such unions are ordered and separated by at least \(c\).  Let \(\widetilde P_n\) be any measurable \(n^{-1}\)-approximate minimum-distance fit in \(\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\):
\[
 \|\widetilde P_n-\widehat P_n\|_\infty
 \leq\inf_{Q\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}}
 \|Q-\widehat P_n\|_\infty+n^{-1}.
\]
Here \(d_H\) denotes the Hausdorff metric induced by the sup norm.  Then \(d_H(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(\widetilde P_n),\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P))\to0\) in probability.  For \(t=3,4\), the minimal ordered interval representation of \(\mathcal I_{k_0,t}^{1\mathrm c}(\widetilde P_n)\) has \(m_t\) components with probability tending to one, and all its lower and upper endpoints converge in probability, in order, to those of \(\mathcal I_{k_0,t}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For each observed cell, the Bernoulli exponential-moment calculation
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\{\lambda(\mathbf 1\{W_r=w\}-P(w))\}\leq e^{\lambda^2/8}
\]
and the elementary inequality \(P\{Z\geq a\}\leq\mathbb E[Z]/a\) for nonnegative \(Z\) give a two-sided probability at most \(2e^{-2n\varepsilon^2}\).  Taking the union over the thirty-two cells implies
\[
 P^n\{\|\widehat P_n-P\|_\infty>\varepsilon\}
 \leq64e^{-2n\varepsilon^2}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{20}
\]
Since the true \(P\) is an admissible competitor in the minimum-distance problem,
\[
 \|\widetilde P_n-P\|_\infty
 \leq\|\widetilde P_n-\widehat P_n\|_\infty+\|\widehat P_n-P\|_\infty
 \leq2\|\widehat P_n-P\|_\infty+n^{-1}.
 \tag{21}
\]
Thus \(\widetilde P_n\to P\) in probability and \(P^n\{\widetilde P_n\in\mathcal V\}\to1\).  An approximate measurable selector can be implemented by fixing a countable dense subset of \(\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), which exists because this class is a subset of the Euclidean simplex, and taking the first enumerated point whose distance is strictly less than the countable infimum plus \(n^{-1}\).  The countable infimum equals the infimum over the model by density and continuity of distance, and this first-index rule is measurable.

The common lower bound on reconstruction denominators makes every \(g_{b(j)}\) jointly continuous, uniformly on the relevant bounded local graphs.  If \(Q_r\to P\), Hausdorff convergence of \(K_j(Q_r)\) therefore gives
\[
 d_H\!\left(g_{b(j)}(Q_r,K_j(Q_r)),g_{b(j)}(P,K_j(P))\right)\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{22}
\]
To verify (22), take any point represented by \(y_r\in K_j(Q_r)\), choose \(y_r^0\in K_j(P)\) at distance at most \(d_H(K_j(Q_r),K_j(P))+r^{-1}\), and use joint uniform continuity; reverse the roles of the two sets for the opposite directed distance.  Since \(J\) is finite, the Hausdorff distance between the unions is bounded by the maximum of the distances in (22).  The dimension-reduction theorem identifies these unions with the two sharp joint images.  Hence the image correspondence is Hausdorff-continuous at \(P\), and (21) proves the first asserted convergence.

For each connected compact \(K_j(Q)\), continuity makes \(\operatorname{proj}_t g_{b(j)}(Q,K_j(Q))\) a compact interval.  Equation (22) and the fact that coordinate projection is one-Lipschitz imply Hausdorff convergence of these scalar intervals.  If compact intervals \([a_r,b_r]\) and \([a,b]\) have Hausdorff distance tending to zero, then \(|a_r-a|\) and \(|b_r-b|\) tend to zero.  Taking finite minima and maxima within each fixed group \(J_{tr}\) proves convergence of that group's two endpoints.  The maintained interval-union condition makes each group one connected component, while the uniform separation and order prevent mergers or reorderings.  Thus the minimal marginal representation has exactly \(m_t\) components locally and all ordered endpoints converge.  Applying this deterministic conclusion on the event \(\widetilde P_n\in\mathcal V\), whose probability tends to one, proves the endpoint assertions.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every rational \(\eta\in(0,3/20)\), every \(k_0\in\mathcal A\), and every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), the signed lists \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\sigma}(P,\eta)\), \(\sigma\in\Sigma\), are observable and finite.  For each \(\sigma\), their sign vectors and complete signed Sturm--Habicht lifting tables are necessary and sufficient for each of the eight oriented systems \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\) to have a real solution.  After the two relative alignments are combined, \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\) is a singleton if and only if every two-copy target-nonconstancy formula is rejected.  Equivalently, every accepted branch cell has zero oscillation in both reconstructed coordinates \(\tau_3\) and \(\tau_4\), and all accepted branch and alignment images coincide.  If this condition fails, the same certificate returns two accepted cells and reconstructed latent witnesses with unequal ATT vectors.  These equivalences include vanishing rank coefficients, alignment coincidences, and every compact-box face.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current universal quantifier over \(P\in\Delta_{31}\) includes laws with \(p_d=0\), at which the conditional tensors \(H_d\) and \(N_d\) are undefined. The proof and the causal singleton claim concern the maintained nonempty exclusive one-collision class, where \(p_d\geq\eta\).

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For fixed \(k_0\in\mathcal A\), \(s\in\{-1,1\}^{3}\), and \(\sigma\in\Sigma\), first impose \(\chi_{0k_0}^{01}=\chi_{0k_0}^{10}=\chi_{0k_0}^{11}=0\) and set
\[
 v_{10k_0}=v_{20k_0}=\frac{N_0(0,0,k_0)}{H_0(0,0,k_0)}.
\]
Retain \(r_{ij}=R_{10}(i,j,k_0)\), set \(R_{20}(i,j,k_0)=H_0(i,j,k_0)-r_{ij}\), and, for each of the other three blocks, set
\[
 R_{1d}(i,j,k)=\frac{N_d(i,j,k)-v_{2dk}H_d(i,j,k)}{v_{1dk}-v_{2dk}},
 \qquad R_{2d}(i,j,k)=H_d(i,j,k)-R_{1d}(i,j,k).
\]
The free coordinate is exactly
\[
 y=(v_{110},v_{210},v_{111},v_{211},v_{10,1-k_0},v_{20,1-k_0},r_{00},r_{01},r_{10},r_{11})\in\mathbb R^{10}.
\]
The system \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\) contains the eight cleared equalities \(\rho_{zdj}(R)=0\), the four cleared equalities \(\gamma_{zi}^{\sigma}(R)=0\), the three strict orientation signs \(s_{dk}(v_{1dk}-v_{2dk})>0\), the inequalities \(R_{zd}(i,j,k)\geq\eta^5\), and both cleared signs \(q-\eta\geq0\) and \(U-q\geq0\) for every reconstructed primitive \(q\).  Reconstruction first uses the arm-local quantities
\[
 T_{zd}^{R}(i,j)=\sum_kR_{zd}(i,j,k),\qquad
 S_{zd}^{R}(i)=\sum_jT_{zd}^{R}(i,j),\qquad
 w_{zd}^{R}=\sum_iS_{zd}^{R}(i),
\]
\[
 u_{zd}^{R}=\frac{S_{zd}^{R}(1)}{w_{zd}^{R}},\qquad
 a_{zdi}^{R}=\frac{T_{zd}^{R}(i,1)}{S_{zd}^{R}(i)},\qquad
 \kappa_{zd3j}^{R}=\frac{R_{zd}(0,j,1)}{T_{zd}^{R}(0,j)}.
\]
It then maps arm-local labels to structural labels by taking treated component \(z\) and control component \(\sigma(z)\):
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 u_{z1}&=u_{z1}^{R},& u_{z0}&=u_{\sigma(z),0}^{R},&
 a_{zi}&=a_{z1i}^{R}=a_{\sigma(z),0,i}^{R},\\
 c_{z3j}&=\kappa_{z1,3,j}^{R},& b_{z3j}&=\kappa_{\sigma(z),0,3,j}^{R},&
 c_{z4k}&=v_{z1k},& b_{z4k}&=v_{\sigma(z),0,k},\\
 \pi_z&=p_0w_{\sigma(z),0}^{R}+p_1w_{z1}^{R},&
 e_z&=\frac{p_1w_{z1}^{R}}{\pi_z}.&&
 \end{aligned}
\]
The equality defining \(a_{zi}\) is imposed by \(\gamma_{zi}^{\sigma}(R)=0\).  The box signs are imposed on all displayed structural primitives, equivalently on the corresponding arm-local primitives before relabeling.  Every cleared denominator is one of the explicitly positive quantities \(H_d,T_{zd}^{R},S_{zd}^{R},w_{zd}^{R},p_d,\pi_z\), or one of the orientation-signed nonzero terminal differences.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: For the relative alignment \(\sigma=\mathrm{sw}\), the former reconstruction combined treated component \(z\) with control component \(\sigma(z)\) when forming \(\pi_z\) but did not apply the same relabeling to \(u_{z0}\), \(b_{z3j}\), and \(b_{z4k}\). The corrected construction makes the arm-local-to-structural label map explicit and therefore reconstructs a single well-typed structural vector on both alignments.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Order \(y\) as displayed in Definition \(\mathrm{def:ten-variable-system}\).  For each \(s\), put into one finite polynomial family every equality polynomial and every weak- or strict-inequality boundary polynomial in \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}\), after clearing only denominators whose positivity is recorded in that system.  At each eliminated coordinate apply the full Collins projection operator to the entire current family: adjoin contents, all coefficients and leading coefficients in that coordinate, discriminants, and resultants and signed principal subresultant coefficients for every unordered pair of distinct current polynomials.  Thus equality--equality, equality--inequality, and inequality--inequality pairs are all projected.  Replace the family by a square-free basis of these projection polynomials and continue recursively through all ten coordinates.  Adjoin the three observable collision minors and the two numerators expressing that the common collided-row terminal probability lies in \([\eta,U]\).

To test target constancy, for every \(s'\) and \(\sigma'\in\Sigma\), form an independent copy \(y'\), put all polynomials from both branch systems into a single family, and adjoin the numerator obtained, after multiplication by a common positive squared denominator, from
\[
 \sum_{t=3}^{4}\left[
 \tau_t\!\left(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,y);P\right)
 -\tau_t\!\left(\operatorname{rec}_{k_0,s',\sigma'}(P,y');P\right)
 \right]^2>0.
\]
Apply the same full-family projection operator to every unordered pair at every stage and eliminate all coordinates in \((y,y')\).  The finite list \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\sigma}(P,\eta)\) is the union, over all eight \(s\), all comparison labels \((s',\sigma')\), and the feasibility and nonconstancy formulas, of the resulting polynomials in the observable cells of \(P\) and \(\eta\).  Its certificate records the sign of every final projection polynomial and the complete signed Sturm--Habicht lifting table, including sections on which a coefficient or resultant vanishes.  Exact sign-invariant lifting decides feasibility and equality of both ATT coordinates across all branches; it retains a sample point for every accepted cell and, for every rejected formula, a finite lifting record in which each candidate cell has a first violated atomic sign.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The former projection family omitted resultants between pairs of structural equality polynomials, so it did not preserve their simultaneous zero set. The corrected construction applies the full projection operator to every unordered pair in the complete current polynomial family, including equality--equality, equality--boundary, and boundary--boundary pairs, in both feasibility and two-copy nonconstancy computations.

proposed.statement: For every rational \(\eta\in(0,3/20)\), every \(k_0\in\mathcal A\), and every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\eta,k_0}^{1\mathrm c}\), the signed lists \(\mathscr L_{k_0,\sigma}(P,\eta)\), \(\sigma\in\Sigma\), are observable and finite.  For each \(\sigma\), their sign vectors and complete signed Sturm--Habicht lifting tables are necessary and sufficient for each of the eight oriented systems \(\mathscr G_{k_0,s,\sigma}(P,\eta;y)\) to have a real solution.  After the two relative alignments are combined, \(\mathcal I_{k_0}^{1\mathrm c}(P)\) is a singleton if and only if every two-copy target-nonconstancy formula is rejected.  Equivalently, every accepted branch cell has zero oscillation in both reconstructed coordinates \(\tau_3\) and \(\tau_4\), and all accepted branch and alignment images coincide.  If this condition fails, the same certificate returns two accepted cells and reconstructed latent witnesses with unequal ATT vectors.  These equivalences include vanishing rank coefficients, alignment coincidences, and every compact-box face.
proposed.justification: On positive-arm one-collision laws, the repaired complete projection and lifting table is an exact necessary-and-sufficient certificate for branch feasibility and ATT point identification.
proposed.gap: The theorem supplies a complete generic algebraic decision certificate after dimension reduction, not a smaller irredundant collection of economically named observable minors; that compression remains open.
proposed.consumer: Applied analyses can certify whether all feasible merger resolutions agree in both ATT coordinates and can retain explicit unequal-ATT witnesses when they do not.

prose_updates.tldr: On the compact binary four-period model, the completed singular result is the exclusive stratum with distinct treated terminal rows and exactly one collided control terminal row. Terminal splitting reduces its forty-coordinate labeled fiber to sixteen ten-variable orientation/alignment charts for each collided state. A corrected full Collins certificate projects every pair in the complete polynomial family and exactly decides branch feasibility and aggregate-ATT constancy, including zero and box-face cells; it is a generic exact certificate, not the still-open compressed economic sign basis. The exact algorithm returns the attained, possibly disconnected sharp image with endpoint witnesses. Full-PMF inversion is uniformly honest in finite samples, and a separate theorem gives Hausdorff and ordered-endpoint consistency under explicit local branch persistence, denominator separation, and component-separation conditions. An injective one-parameter family has two separated quotient ATT values, proving positive-dimensional persistence but not relative openness in a larger collision variety.

project_justification.gap: Ahn--Kasahara's parameter and ATT identification results impose their stated regular conditions, while Higgins and Jochmans require rank, type-separation, and connectivity conditions. Neither classifies aggregate ATT on the exclusive one-collided-control-row fiber. General Collins quantifier elimination can decide polynomial formulas, but an incomplete projection subfamily cannot certify simultaneous structural equalities, and generic CAD does not itself supply the causal chart reduction or a compressed economic diagnostic.
project_justification.niche: Exactly one collided control terminal row is the first completed nonregular stratum here: full-path terminal splitting, rank failure, compact-box contact, and the two relative cross-arm alignments interact but reduce to ten coordinates. The result deliberately does not claim the other fifteen terminal-collision patterns of a global atlas.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the corrected arm-label-aware ten-coordinate reconstruction, uses a complete all-pairs Collins projection certificate to classify feasibility and point identification on that stratum, computes its exact attained ATT image, supplies finite-sample full-PMF coverage, and derives Hausdorff and ordered-endpoint consistency under explicit local branch-continuity conditions. A separate injective one-parameter family proves persistent two-value ambiguity. Compression of the complete certificate to a smaller irredundant observable basis remains open.

prose_updates.related_work: Ahn--Kasahara is the closest econometric comparator in the same full-path latent-transition architecture; its regular identification results motivate the estimand and factorization here. The compact class \(\mathcal M_\eta\) and its exclusive one-collision stratum are not asserted to equal, contain, or extend that published identification class. Higgins and Jochmans give a four-observation Markov-mixture benchmark under rank, separation, and connectivity conditions but do not classify a two-arm one-collision alignment fiber. Critch motivates algebraic treatment of binary hidden Markov laws but has neither treatment-arm alignment nor this causal functional. Geiger--Meek and Collins provide generic real quantifier elimination; after correction, the paper uses the complete all-pairs projection machinery only after its model-specific forty-to-ten reduction and claims no generic complexity gain or compressed sign basis. Duarte and coauthors motivate polynomial causal bounds, whereas the object here is an exact attained semialgebraic image. Romano--Shaikh motivates identified-set inference; the present finite-sample inversion is auxiliary, while the separate consistency theorem states the additional local branch conditions needed for Hausdorff and endpoint convergence.
prose_updates.interpretation: A reported ATT sign on this merger stratum is identified only when the complete two-copy certificate rejects every feasible unequal-ATT pair across all orientations and both relative alignments. Otherwise the estimand is the attained set itself, which may be disconnected and must not be replaced by its convex hull. The exact certificate is suitable as a backend audit trail; a short economically interpretable front-end diagnostic remains an open compression problem.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The completed algebra covers only laws whose entire compact fiber has distinct treated terminal rows and exactly one specified collided control terminal row. The certificate has now been repaired to project equality--equality and every other polynomial pair, but it remains full Collins quantifier elimination and may have its generic worst-case cost. The endpoint theorem is local and conditional on a persistent finite branch-component decomposition, Hausdorff-continuous feasible components, uniformly separated reconstruction denominators, and stable separated marginal component groups. The positive-dimensional benchmark is one explicit affine family and is not claimed relatively open in the full collision variety.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Completed claims are quotient invariance, the corrected forty-to-ten one-collision reduction, the complete thirty-two-branch feasibility and ATT-constancy certificate across both collided states, the exact attained stratum-restricted region, the explicit positive-dimensional two-value family, uniformly honest finite-sample full-PMF inversion, and branch-conditional Hausdorff and ordered-endpoint consistency. No result is claimed for the other terminal-collision strata, for an unboxed singular class, for a global sixteen-collision-pattern atlas, or for relative openness of the benchmark family. The complete certificate is not advertised as the model-specific compressed vanishing/sign test requested by the broader agenda; strict sufficient and irredundant compression remains the open question. No overlap, inclusion, or extension relation with Ahn--Kasahara's regular identification class is claimed.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem gives the auditable structural reduction for the exclusive one-collided-control-row fiber and now makes the swapped control-to-treated label map explicit.
statement_notes.gap: Generic elimination does not expose the six terminal coordinates, four collided-prefix splits, eight rank-one equations, four cross-arm alignment equations, or the exact sixteen branches for a fixed collided state.
statement_notes.consumer: A checker for the public \(ak\) package can reconstruct both relative alignments without silently pairing treated type \(z\) with the wrong control primitives.

statement_notes.justification: On positive-arm one-collision laws, the repaired complete projection and lifting table is an exact necessary-and-sufficient certificate for branch feasibility and ATT point identification.
statement_notes.gap: The theorem supplies a complete generic algebraic decision certificate after dimension reduction, not a smaller irredundant collection of economically named observable minors; that compression remains open.
statement_notes.consumer: Applied analyses can certify whether all feasible merger resolutions agree in both ATT coordinates and can retain explicit unequal-ATT witnesses when they do not.

statement_notes.justification: Complete projection after the ten-coordinate reduction returns the attained causal region without convexifying disconnected components.
statement_notes.gap: General CAD does not itself provide this corrected causal reconstruction, fixed branch inventory, or latent endpoint-witness grammar.
statement_notes.consumer: The public \(ak\) backend can report exact marginal components, algebraic endpoints, and a feasible representation attaining each reported boundary.

statement_notes.justification: This auxiliary appendix-tier theorem covers the entire disconnected identified set uniformly at every sample size by inverting the full empirical PMF.
statement_notes.gap: Finite-sample outer coverage alone does not imply branch persistence or set-estimation consistency; those conclusions require the separate explicit continuity conditions.
statement_notes.consumer: Applied analyses obtain honest simultaneous coverage of both marginal sets without selecting one latent alignment.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem separates finite-sample coverage from estimation and supplies Hausdorff and ordered-endpoint consistency under checkable local branch-component conditions.
statement_notes.gap: At merger boundaries, empirical laws may activate or delete branches and split or merge marginal components, so consistency cannot be inferred from a shrinking confidence radius alone.
statement_notes.consumer: Software can diagnose denominator separation and persistent component order before interpreting plug-in algebraic endpoints as consistent estimates.
